findings.message: "_guardCounter" is written by the reentrancy guard `nonReentrant` on every call to stakeWithPermit, stake, withdraw, getReward. Consider OpenZeppelin's ReentrancyGuardTransient, which keeps the lock in transient storage (EIP-1153) instead of a storage slot. MonadLens does not count this as contention; measure the function to see whether the slot shows up as hot.

findings.message: "totalSupply" accumulates a per-call amount in _mint, so every caller reads and writes the same slot.

"totalSupply" is written in _burn, and _burn is only called from burn (via _update), which also writes "reserve0" and "reserve1". Those calls already serialize on the reserves, so this adds no contention of its own; no fix is offered.

"unlocked" is written by the reentrancy guard `lock` on every call to mint, burn, swap, skim, sync. Consider OpenZeppelin's ReentrancyGuardTransient, which keeps the lock in transient storage (EIP-1153) instead of a storage slot. MonadLens does not count this as contention; measure the function to see whether the slot shows up as hot.

"price0CumulativeLast" is written in _update, and _update also writes "reserve0" and "reserve1". Those calls already serialize on the reserves, so this adds no contention of its own; no fix is offered.

"price1CumulativeLast" is written in _update, and _update also writes "reserve0" and "reserve1". Those calls already serialize on the reserves, so this adds no contention of its own; no fix is offered.
"reserve0" is updated by every _update on this pool. This contention is inherent: sharding it would break the pool's pricing invariant, so no fix is offered.
